title: "Search and ranking"
subtitle: "Planned (step 4): a search over edits ordered by a learned ranker, measured in calls to the local solver."

::: {.callout-note title="Partly built"}
The plan was agreed on Nov 7, 2026. Since then the teacher search has run
(Nov 8–9) and the CMGMP baseline has been evaluated; the ranker is not
trained yet, and a redesign of the search, decided on Nov 9, is being
implemented ([below](#redesign)).
:::

## The search

A node is a simulated state, identified by its formation, the disk's
connected region and the box's pose within a certified radius
([Node identity](node-identity.qmd)). From a node, the candidates are
the edits that pass [the hold gate](hold-gate.qmd); each expansion calls the
[local solver](local-solver.qmd) Λ, which is the expensive part. The search
is policy-guided (Levin tree search, or policy-guided heuristic search): a
ranker gives a probability π to each candidate edit, nodes are expanded in
order of depth divided by the probability of their path, Λ is charged when
a node is expanded, and edits the gate rejects get π = 0. For this order,
Orseau and Lelis bound the number of expansions by depth / probability of
the solution. The theory note extends the bound to duplicate states (with the
safe duplicate rule and the node key of [Node identity](node-identity.qmd))
and to a Λ that fails at random (with restarts).

## The ranker

- **Inputs:** one token per contact template (type, gap, normal,
  contact-set length, whether it is on), one per body, and one for the goal;
  attention across tokens, with learned biases for pairs that are related by
  containment or share a body or an environment element.
- **Output:** a score per candidate edit, normalized over the candidates into
  π.
- **Training:** supervised, from searches that call Λ without guidance on
  many scene instances: the policy-guided-search loss on solution paths, plus
  a cross-entropy on whether each Λ call succeeded.
- **Baselines:** search without guidance; the gate's margin as the score; and
  a learned feasibility classifier with uniform-cost search on −Σ ln P
  (Hauser, Bretl and Latombe, ICRA 2005).

## Scene families

| Family | Scene and goal |
|---|---|
| F1. Step, randomized | step height, box size, friction, starts; goals on the platform; also lowering the box from the platform |
| F2. Staircase | two or three steps of random rise and tread |
| F3. Wall and ledge | topple the box against a wall, or lift it onto a ledge beside it |

One disk for now. The families come after the redesign below works on the
step, and a second disk after that (decided Nov 9). Validity is computed from the geometry for each family
([Issues](issues.qmd#validity)).

**Teacher search: the first full run (Nov 8–9).** The pipeline generates
seeded step instances, runs the search with a teacher ranker, and logs every Λ
call with the gate's verdicts as training data for the ranker. Its first small
check solved none; the transfers it failed were real realizer failures (makes
that never reached the contact, disk transfers planned as a retreat, contacts
placed at feature ends, hand-overs lingering in a tie), and the fixed realizer
accepts 51 of the 76 it had failed. The full run (200 instances; the relaxed
gate, the learned break skill, retries from other nodes of a key):

| Task | Solved | Λ calls per solve |
|---|---|---|
| Disk contact on the box's side (sub-goal) | 40/40 | 5.1 |
| Box flush on the riser (sub-goal) | 40/40 | 17.5 |
| The pivot formation (sub-goal) | 39/40 | 18.8 |
| Lift onto the platform | 0/40 | — |
| Lower to the floor | 0/40 | — |

7,795 Λ calls (4,954 accepted) are recorded as training data
(`cmg/scripts/step4/teacher/results/t-full/merged/`). Lifting has since been
solved in 5 of 10 instances with a second learned skill
([the local solver](local-solver.qmd#learned-skill)). Lowering is open: the
only edit off the platform, onto the step corner, is a balance Λ<sub>qs</sub>
can't hold (0/52, tried in the 11 instances whose box started 0.6–32.8 mm
from the edge), and nothing brings a box farther away to the edge. Six of the
52 calls dropped the box into the lowering goal, in 3 of the 40 instances, and
were rejected because they didn't end in the requested formation; the
redesign keeps such outcomes ([below](#redesign)).

**Baseline: the contact-mode-guided planner (CMGMP).** Built from the authors'
code without root (in a container on Juno) and patched for the disk's 1 N
limit. Its plan for lowering, executed in our simulator and graded by the same
strict test, **succeeds**: the box comes off the platform and rests flat on
the floor.

**Evaluated on 50 shared test starts** (25 per task; 60 s per start on one
CPU core, with restarts; settings chosen on 10 separate tuning starts; every
plan executed in our MJX simulator and graded by the same strict test):

| Task | Plan returned | Strict success | 95% CI | Median time to success |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lift | 11/25 | **6/25** | 11–43% | 45.2 s |
| Lower | 25/25 | **19/25** | 57–89% | 39.4 s |

Lift plans are rare, and half of them fail in execution because the box doesn't
hold the goal; lower plans come easily, but 50 of 71 executions don't hold the
goal, and retries within the budget give 19/25.

**Not yet a paired comparison.** Our planner lifts 5/10 with the learned
skills (7/10 with the proposed tie rule) and lowers none, but on different
instances and with a budget counted in Λ calls. So far the baseline is ahead on
lowering, ours on lifting. Our lift instances 0–9 happen to be CMGMP's first 10
lift starts (ours 5/10, or 7/10 with the tie rule; CMGMP 2/10), but under
different success criteria and budgets, so that is not the comparison either.

**The paired comparison's protocol** (decided Nov 9; run after the redesign):
the same 50 starts (25 lift, 25 lower); the same goal test and the same strict
grading of every plan executed in MJX; a matched wall-clock budget per start on
the same hardware class; no retries in our planner; Wilson intervals and
McNemar's test on the paired outcomes; both planners' plan-found and
executed-success rates reported.

*Caveats:* the baseline plans quasi-statically with a point finger, while
execution is dynamic with soft contacts; moves between its planned contacts are
tracked along straight lines without collision planning, so some execution
failures may be the executor's; its 1 N limit is applied per contact component
(up to about 1.4 N along a world axis); and its contact-mode code was patched for
the box wedged into the floor–riser corner.

**Built (Nov 8): the validity tables for all three families.** The builder
now takes any polygonal environment and a rectangular box. It reproduces the
step's tables exactly, and built the two new families (default dimensions;
random-instance ranges are documented, not yet sampled):

| | Step | F2 staircase (2 steps) | F3 wall and ledge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certified valid formations | 357 | 649 | 473 |
| Nodes of W (recognizable, vertex–vertex only alone) | 328 | 592 | 443 |
| Excluded sets | 560 pairs + 1 triple | 1,624 pairs + 5 triples | 840 pairs + 10 triples |
| Compound edges (local rule, ρ = 25 mm) | 92 | 172 | 144 |

New in the families: concave corners the box can wedge into (80 staircase
formations, 42 wall-and-ledge), and pivot-like compound edges at every convex
corner. Neither has collinear edges, so the "pit" case of the theory note
doesn't arise yet.

**The test:** a 2 × 2 table of transfer, holding out an environment family
(F3) and holding out the number of disks (once a second disk is built), with cost measured in Λ calls. A
targeted literature search found learned guidance for contact or mode search
tested on held-out instances, objects, object counts or robot counts, but
not on a held-out family of environments; the closest work counts solver
calls with learned feasibility for pick-and-place (Ortiz-Haro et al., ICRA
2023).

## The redesign (Decision 23, Nov 9) {#redesign}

**Why.** The search throws away motions that make progress but don't end in
the requested contact state. Asked to lift the box's floor corner, Λ<sub>qs</sub>
instead tilts the box from about 10° to 67° while keeping all three contacts.
The call fails, but the box is now where a short route lifts it without any
learned skill: move the disk under the box, then push it over the step corner
([the video](../results/index.qmd)).

**What changes** (implemented Nov 9 and now the defaults; evaluated on 40
lift and 40 lower instances, see [the results](../results/index.qmd#d23-results)):

- **Outcome children.** A call yields at most one child, labelled by the state
  it actually reaches. The child is accepted if it is the requested state, or
  if it lowers a value estimate by at least δ = 10 mm.
- **Two new actions,** each with its own gate: moving the box *within* its
  contact state, and **releases**, where the box is let go and comes to rest in
  the next state. Lowering becomes a push toward the platform's edge, then a
  release to the floor. The final roll onto the platform becomes a release
  too, so the tie rule and the roll skill are shelved.
- **The order of the search** is PHS\* (Orseau and Lelis 2021), with its
  heuristic factor η from a value function, clipped to [1, η<sub>max</sub>]
  (η<sub>max</sub> = 10 to start; 4, 10 and 30 to be measured).
- **The value.** To start, 𝒱₀: the distance to the goal in the edit graph plus
  the box's distance to a fixed set of poses where the next edit passes the
  gate. Then one learned value V₁, the expected number of Λ calls to the
  goal, trained by temporal differences on every logged call, failures
  included (a call that succeeds with probability p costs about 1/p calls).
  The distance to the goal enters only as shaping and as an input.
- **Smaller decisions.** The 125 mm gap screen (Near) is dropped: the gate and
  box transport decide, and distance only orders the candidates. The disk's
  clearance check stays, as part of the gate. Duplicate pruning also compares
  calls per path probability. The approach lasts as long as its path needs.
  The settle clause is off for formation edits and required for releases and
  the final goal state. Retries (2 per node) are for the teacher only; the
  planner and every reported result use none. The search keeps popping
  batches, and a batched version of the call bound is being proved.

**Since Nov 10** (decided with Aykut, one at a time):

- **The goal push aims at the goal window's centre** (default). Aiming at the
  nearest goal pose, the window's edge, left boxes a few mm short and stuck:
  15 against 13 of 16 end-to-end instances, paired, no losses.
- **The push gate** (default): a box move is refused when no disk placement on
  the face can push the box along the planned path (a linear program at five
  poses). A paired check is running; shortening an unpushable push to its last
  pushable pose is built behind a flag.
- **Which ends count.** An end with the disk outside its workspace (the
  joint ranges) is invalid; quasi-static runs reject ends reached through a
  dynamic event, and other runs tag and count them.
- **The value.** V₁ and the ranker are retrained on the full lift goal (V₁'s
  error on lift-goal pairs 1.03 → 0.33 calls). V₁ enters only η, as
  1 + k̂/g, behind a flag. Acceptance stays on 𝒱₀ with δ = 10 mm, which is
  derived from the merge radius, not chosen; V₁ takes over acceptance once it
  has a certified Lipschitz bound, and an exploration loop is to follow.

**The release route, tested first** (84 starts, the break states the teacher
search reached; `cmg/scripts/step4/release_test/`, commit `12fc963`):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s "failed" break keeps all three contacts | 84/84, tilt about 10° → 67° |
| The route end to end, Λ<sub>qs</sub> as it was | 2/84 |
| Why: with the disk away, the box creeps in MJX (about 0.5°/s) while each approach lasted 16.2 s | box slid off the step corner in 80/84 |
| The route with a short approach: the next two edits reach their states | 84/84 |
| The release push, stop when the box is fully on the platform: at rest, fully on | **76/84** (82–95%) |

From these: the approach now lasts only as long as its path needs (`3c52753`);
the release realizer is the push with the "fully on" stop; the box counts as at
rest within 1 mm and about 15 mrad (MJX shows a small periodic tilt cycle at
rest, up to 12.5 mrad); simulator settings are being tested for the creep. One
problem remains: the strict test rejects the step that brings the disk under
the box (84/84), because the approach path brushes the box. The path is being
fixed; how the recognizer reads such brushes is queued for a separate
rethink.
